title: Practice Exam 2
description: A second full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: You are towing a small utility trailer on a freeway posted at 65 mph. Your maximum legal speed is:
choices: 55 mph
65 mph
60 mph
Whatever the posted limit says
questions.explanation: Vehicles towing a trailer—and trucks with three or more axles—are limited to 55 mph in California, even where cars may legally go 65.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Speed Limits for Trailers

questions.question: You drive into a blind intersection (one with no stop sign or signal where buildings block your view). You may not exceed:
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
20 mph
10 mph
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection the limit is 15 mph during the last 100 feet, unless you can see at least 100 feet in both directions. The same 15 mph applies in alleys and at unguarded rail crossings.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: A round (circular) highway sign is used specifically to warn of:
choices: A railroad crossing ahead
A roundabout ahead
A no-passing zone
A one-way road
questions.explanation: The round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead—slow, look, and listen. A horizontal-triangle pennant warns of no-passing zones; other meanings use other shapes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sign Shapes

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass and you are in a no-passing zone on a two-lane road. You should:
choices: Maintain a steady speed and let them decide; do not speed up
Speed up so they cannot pass at all
Wave them around even though it is a no-passing zone
Brake hard to discourage them
questions.explanation: Never speed up when being passed, and don't encourage an illegal pass. Keep a steady speed (or ease off slightly) so the situation resolves safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Being Passed

questions.question: You are turning left at a green light (no arrow). Oncoming traffic is heavy. You should:
choices: Enter the intersection and wait, completing the turn only when it is clear and safe
Turn immediately because the green gives you the right of way
Wait behind the limit line until the light turns red, then turn
Force your way through to keep traffic moving
questions.explanation: On a solid green you may enter the intersection to wait, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and complete the turn only when there is a safe gap—even if that's as the light changes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Left Turns

questions.question: At a T-intersection with no signs, the road you are on ends at a through road. You must:
choices: Yield to all traffic on the through road before entering or turning
Proceed first if you arrived first
Go straight across without yielding
Assume through traffic will stop for you
questions.explanation: Traffic on the through road (the top of the T) has the right of way. The driver on the ending road must yield to it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right-of-Way at Intersections

questions.question: Which lane-change procedure is in the correct order?
choices: Signal, check mirrors, check the blind spot over your shoulder, then steer over
Steer over, then signal, then check mirrors
Check the blind spot, steer over, then signal
Signal and steer over at the same time
questions.explanation: Signal first to warn others, scan your mirrors, do a head-check of the blind spot, and only then move—steering before checking is how blind-spot collisions happen.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean:
choices: Neither direction may cross to pass; you may cross only to turn left into a driveway or street
Passing is allowed for both directions
The road is one-way
You may cross any time to pass slow vehicles
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing for both directions. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side street when safe.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pavement Markings

questions.question: You are following a motorcycle on a wet road. Compared with following a car, you should:
choices: Allow more following distance, because motorcycles can stop very quickly
Allow less distance, because motorcycles are smaller
Keep the same 3-second gap as for a car
Tailgate so other cars don't cut between you
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop in a shorter distance than cars, and wet roads add risk. Increase your following distance to 4+ seconds to give yourself room to react.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance

questions.question: Doubling your speed from 25 to 50 mph affects your braking distance by roughly:
choices: Quadrupling it—it grows much faster than speed does
Doubling it—proportional to speed
Leaving it about the same
Increasing it by half
questions.explanation: Braking distance increases with the square of speed, so doubling speed roughly quadruples the distance needed to stop. This is why small speed increases sharply raise crash risk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stopping Distances

questions.question: A driver under 21 is stopped and registers a BAC of 0.02%. Under California's zero-tolerance law:
choices: They are in violation; the limit for under-21 drivers is 0.01%
They are legal, since it is under 0.08%
They are legal, since it is under 0.05%
It only matters if they were weaving
questions.explanation: For drivers under 21 the limit is 0.01%—essentially any measurable alcohol. 0.02% exceeds it and leads to license suspension, regardless of driving behavior.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Zero Tolerance Law

questions.question: You take an over-the-counter cold medicine labeled 'may cause drowsiness' and then drive. If your driving is impaired, you:
choices: Can be arrested for DUI, even though the medicine is legal
Cannot be charged because no alcohol is involved
Are fine as long as you took the normal dose
Are only at risk if it was a prescription drug
questions.explanation: DUI applies to any drug—legal, prescription, or over-the-counter—that impairs your driving. Always heed drowsiness warnings before getting behind the wheel.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Drugs and Driving

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you on a divided highway is stopped with red lights flashing, but a raised median separates your side from the bus. You:
choices: May proceed with caution without stopping, because the road is divided by a barrier
Must stop, because the bus lights are flashing red
Must stop only if children are visible
Must stop and wait for the bus to move first
questions.explanation: On a divided highway with a raised median or barrier, traffic on the opposite side need not stop for a school bus. On an undivided road, both directions must stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Buses

questions.question: A school zone is posted '25 MPH WHEN CHILDREN ARE PRESENT.' At 7 p.m. with no children anywhere in sight, you:
choices: May drive the normal street speed limit, since no children are present
Must always drive 25 mph in that block
Must drive 15 mph regardless
Must stop before entering the zone
questions.explanation: The reduced limit on this sign applies only when children are present. With none around, the regular speed limit applies—but stay alert, as children can appear quickly.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Zones

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with siren on is approaching, but you are already in the middle of an intersection. You should:
choices: Continue through, clear the intersection, then pull to the right and stop
Stop immediately where you are in the intersection
Back up out of the intersection
Turn left quickly to get away
questions.explanation: Never stop in an intersection. Clear it first, then pull to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: A fire engine is racing ahead of you with siren and lights on. The closest you may legally follow it is:
choices: More than 300 feet behind
100 feet behind
50 feet behind
Any distance, if you stay in your lane
questions.explanation: You may not follow within 300 feet of any emergency vehicle that has its siren or lights operating. Trailing closely interferes with its movement and is illegal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: A pedestrian who began crossing on a 'WALK' signal is still in the crosswalk when it changes to a flashing upraised hand and your light turns green. You:
choices: Must let them finish crossing before you proceed
May proceed because your light is green
May proceed because their signal is no longer 'WALK'
Should honk so they hurry across
questions.explanation: Pedestrians lawfully in the crosswalk keep the right of way until they finish crossing, even after the signal changes. You must wait.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrian Signals

questions.question: You intend to turn right at a corner that has a bike lane. The correct procedure is to:
choices: Signal, check for cyclists, then merge into the bike lane within 200 feet of the corner before turning
Turn right from the regular lane, crossing the bike lane during the turn
Stop in the traffic lane and turn without entering the bike lane
Speed up to turn ahead of any approaching cyclist
questions.explanation: Merging into the bike lane within 200 feet of the corner (after yielding to cyclists) keeps you from cutting across a cyclist's path mid-turn—the 'right hook' crash.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicycle Lanes

questions.question: You see a curb painted blue. You may park there only if:
choices: Your vehicle displays a valid disabled-person placard or plate
You will be gone less than five minutes
You are loading passengers
It is after business hours
questions.explanation: Blue curbs are reserved for vehicles displaying a valid disabled placard or plate. Parking there without one is illegal regardless of how briefly you stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: After parallel parking on the right side of a two-way street, your tires must be within how far of the curb?
choices: 18 inches
3 feet
2 feet
6 inches
questions.explanation: Your wheels must end up within 18 inches of the curb. Parking too far out exposes your car to traffic and is a citable offense.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parallel Parking

questions.question: On a multi-lane freeway, slower drivers should generally keep right because the left lane is intended for:
choices: Passing and faster-moving traffic
Trucks and towed loads
Vehicles preparing to exit
Carpools only, at all times
questions.explanation: Keep right except to pass. The left lane is for passing and faster traffic; lingering there while slower than surrounding traffic impedes flow and can be cited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Choosing a Lane

questions.question: You realize you are about to miss your freeway exit. You should:
choices: Go on to the next exit and turn around there
Stop and back up on the shoulder to reach the exit
Cut sharply across lanes at the last second
Stop in the gore (striped) area and reverse into the ramp
questions.explanation: Never stop, back up, or make sudden multi-lane moves on a freeway. Continue to the next exit—missing one is a minor inconvenience compared with causing a crash.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Leaving the Freeway

questions.question: A 17-year-old wants to use a hands-free phone to make a call while driving. Under California law they:
choices: May not use any wireless device while driving, even hands-free
May use it because it is hands-free
May use it only on local streets
May use it for calls but not texts
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 are prohibited from using any wireless device while driving—hands-free included—except to report a genuine emergency.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Teen Cell Phone Restrictions

questions.question: Which is the clearest example of a distraction that is both visual AND manual?
choices: Reaching down to pick up a dropped phone and looking for it
Listening to a podcast
Talking with a hands-free headset
Daydreaming about your day
questions.explanation: Reaching for an object takes your eyes (visual) and a hand (manual) off driving at once. Cognitive distractions like daydreaming take only your mind; the combined ones are most dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Types of Distraction

questions.question: A green left-turn arrow then changes to a steady green ball (no arrow). This means:
choices: You may still turn left, but must now yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
You may no longer turn left
Your protected turn continues unchanged
You must stop and wait for the arrow again
questions.explanation: The arrow gave you a protected turn; once it becomes a plain green, oncoming traffic also has a green, so you may turn only when you can yield safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Arrows

questions.question: At a red light you wish to turn right. A posted sign reads 'NO TURN ON RED.' You may:
choices: Not turn until the light is green
Turn right after a complete stop, as usual
Turn right if no pedestrians are present
Turn right if traffic is clear and you signal
questions.explanation: Although right-on-red is normally allowed after stopping, a 'NO TURN ON RED' sign overrides it. You must wait for the green.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Right Turn on Red

questions.question: A flashing yellow ARROW at a left-turn pocket means:
choices: You may turn left, but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first
You have a protected left turn
Left turns are not allowed
Stop, then turn as at a stop sign
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow permits a left turn but is unprotected—oncoming traffic has a green. Yield, then turn when safe. A steady green arrow would be protected.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Flashing Yellow Arrow

questions.question: You want to make a U-turn in a residential district. It is legal when:
choices: No vehicle is approaching within 200 feet and no sign prohibits it
Any time, as long as you signal
Only at a green light
Only if you are within 100 feet of a corner
questions.explanation: In a residential area a U-turn is legal if no car is coming within 200 feet and it isn't prohibited by a sign. Never U-turn near a curve or hilltop where you can't see 200 feet, or in front of a fire station.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — U-Turns

questions.question: A white diamond symbol painted on the pavement of a lane indicates:
choices: A carpool / HOV lane, usable only by qualifying vehicles during posted hours
A lane that is ending ahead
A lane reserved for trucks
A bicycle lane
questions.explanation: The diamond marks an HOV (carpool) lane. Only vehicles meeting the posted occupancy requirement may use it during the hours shown; a separate sign lists the rules.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Carpool Lanes

questions.question: You park facing downhill next to a curb. You should turn the front wheels:
choices: Toward the curb, so a forward roll is stopped by the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Toward the center of the road
questions.explanation: Downhill (with or without a curb), point the wheels toward the curb/edge so a rolling car turns into the curb instead of into traffic. Set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: An orange-colored sign or cone in a work area tells you:
choices: You are in or approaching a construction/maintenance zone—reduce speed and watch for workers
There is a scenic viewpoint ahead
A school crossing is ahead
The road surface is freshly paved and smooth
questions.explanation: Orange means construction or maintenance. Expect lane shifts, workers, and equipment; slow down and obey any reduced limits—fines are often doubled here.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Construction Zones

questions.question: You are caught speeding in a clearly marked construction zone while workers are present. Compared with a normal ticket, the fine is:
choices: Often doubled
Reduced because work zones are temporary
Exactly the same
Waived for first offenses
questions.explanation: Traffic fines are frequently doubled in active work zones to protect workers. Slow down and stay alert wherever orange signs and cones appear.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Work Zone Penalties

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with certain prescription medications usually:
choices: Multiplies the impairment—more dangerous than either alone
Cancels out the effects of both
Has no effect if doses are small
Only matters for drivers over 65
questions.explanation: Alcohol and many medications interact, intensifying drowsiness and impairment far beyond either by itself. Combining them before driving is especially hazardous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Combining Alcohol and Drugs

questions.question: A bicyclist ahead of you signals and moves toward the center of the lane to turn left. You should:
choices: Treat the cyclist like any vehicle turning left and yield; do not pass on the left
Pass quickly on the left before they turn
Honk so they return to the bike lane
Pass on the right shoulder
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may take the lane to turn left, just like cars. Yield and give them room; passing on the left as they turn is dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicyclists Turning

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, the size of gap you should aim for in traffic is about:
choices: A four-second gap, so you and nearby cars have room to adjust
One car length
A half-second gap to keep up momentum
Whatever gap exists when you reach the end of the ramp
questions.explanation: Aim for at least a four-second gap when merging. Matching traffic speed and choosing a roomy gap lets everyone adjust smoothly instead of braking hard.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Merging Onto Freeways

questions.question: After completing a lane change, your signal is still blinking. Leaving it on can be dangerous because:
choices: Other drivers may think you intend to turn or change lanes again
It drains the battery quickly
It is illegal to signal for more than 10 seconds
It disables your brake lights
questions.explanation: A signal left on misleads others into expecting a turn or lane change, which can cause them to brake or yield unexpectedly. Cancel it once your maneuver is done.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Using Turn Signals
